section_summary: This section finishes a SCAP call-sign supplement for Japanese ship and coastal radio stations, then presents State Department correspondence on Japanese radio policy, interference complaints, ship-to-shore service, international broadcasting, and the use of Japanese call signs in the Ryukyu Islands. It also contains inquiries about the Kyodo radio station, a civilian recollection of a Japanese broadcast before Pearl Harbor, and diplomatic exchanges concerning the resumption of Japanese international broadcasting. The final pages begin the July 1949 official directory of Japanese standard-frequency, coastal, radiobeacon, and ship radio stations, including extensive technical schedules and registry tables.

subfiles.title: Call Sign Supplement: Japanese Ship and Coastal Radio Stations
subfiles.from: Japanese Ministry of Communications under SCAP authorization
subfiles.about: Lists ship-radio registrations and records additions, deletions, and changes to Japanese station call signs and technical assignments.
subfiles.summary: The continuing registry identifies fishing and other vessels by SCAP number, port, tonnage, operational agency, call sign, authorized frequencies, power, and emission type. The closing portions enumerate call-sign additions, deletions, and changes for ship stations. A final technical section records changes for coastal and radiobeacon stations, including Tsunoshima, Kiritappu, and Kushirozaki.

subfiles.title: Use in Ryukyu Islands of Radio Call Letters Allocated to Japan
subfiles.from: W. E. O'Connor, Telecommunications Division
subfiles.about: Records the Department's advice that SCAP could provisionally use Japanese call letters in the Ryukyu Islands.
subfiles.summary: Major Holliman asked whether State objected to moving the JSA-JSZ call letters to the Ryukyus; as the islands legally remain part of Japan pending a settlement, MacArthur may treat them so.

subfiles.title: Inquiry concerning the Japanese Kyodo radio station
subfiles.from: Julius Mate Jr.
subfiles.about: Requests information about the Japanese Kyodo radio station, formerly associated with Domei.
subfiles.summary: Julius Mate Jr. of Flint, Michigan asks about the former Domei, now Kyodo, radio station.

subfiles.title: Reply to Julius Mate Jr. concerning Kyodo
subfiles.from: Francis Colt de Wolf, Department of State
subfiles.about: Provides limited information about Kyodo's international press traffic and invites a more specific inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Department says the Kyodo station carries press traffic between Japan and foreign countries, apparently used by United Press, and invites Mate to ask more specific questions.

subfiles.title: Complaint of interference to Lisbon station CUJ-2
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Requests investigation of suspected Japanese interference with reception of Lisbon station CUJ-2 in London.
subfiles.summary: Airgram: British authorities say a teleprinter with call sign JFI on about 15961.9 kHz interfered with Lisbon's CUJ-2; the Portuguese assignment had priority; Tokyo asked to investigate.

subfiles.title: FCC referral of the CUJ-2 interference complaint, with enclosures
subfiles.from: T. J. Slowie, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.to: Francis C. de Wolf, Department of State
subfiles.about: Transmits British monitoring reports and FCC measurements concerning interference between JFI and CUJ-2.
subfiles.summary: FCC refers the CUJ-2 interference complaint with London's message and US monitoring measurements, and sends diplomatic handling to State.

subfiles.title: Japanese ship-to-shore radio service since April 1947
subfiles.from: Francis Colt de Wolf, Department of State
subfiles.to: T. M. Stevens, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.about: Summarizes postwar rules and extensions of Japanese ship-to-shore radio service.
subfiles.summary: Letter on Japanese ship-to-shore service since April 1947: October 1947 changes allow certain full-rate messages for US ships, coastal stations keep distress watches, service extended to Norwegian and Dutch vessels, with rates and accounting rules.

subfiles.title: Treatment of Japanese broadcasting requirements in the U.S. draft frequency plan
subfiles.from: George E. Sterling, U.S. delegation, Mexico City
subfiles.about: Requests policy guidance on Japan's extensive domestic and international high-frequency broadcasting requirements.
subfiles.summary: US delegation summarizes Japan's requests for 114 channel-hours of domestic and 165.5 of international broadcasting; Sterling proposes reasonable domestic needs, minimal Asian international service and little for the Americas, Europe and Africa.

subfiles.title: Tokyo response on alleged JFI interference
subfiles.from: USPOLAD, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports that neither the U.S. Army Tokyo circuit nor a Japanese JFI station could plausibly have caused the reported interference.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo reply: the Army Tokyo-Manila transmitter on 15955 kHz was not operating or using JFI; a Japanese JFI assignment is on 2540 kHz without radioteletype; London should recheck the offender.

subfiles.title: Advice to London concerning the CUJ-2 interference source
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Advises that the interfering transmitter was believed to be a U.S. airline station under contract to Iceland.
subfiles.summary: Department reports the CUJ-2 interference appeared to come from a US airline, so the complaint should go to Iceland.

subfiles.title: Correction of the erroneous identification of a Japanese station
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Notifies Tokyo that the interfering station had been wrongly identified as Japanese.
subfiles.summary: Department states the interfering call sign was not JFI and military authorities are to be told the Japanese identification was erroneous.

subfiles.title: Follow-up questions about the Kyodo radio station
subfiles.from: Julius Mate Jr.
subfiles.about: Asks five specific questions about the former Domei or Kyodo radio station.
subfiles.summary: Mate asks when Domei or Kyodo ceased, where it was, its listening area, ownership and call letters.

subfiles.title: Internal note on the Mate inquiry
subfiles.from: H. O. Briggs, Telecommunications Division
subfiles.about: Records Major Holliman's view that Mate's motives for requesting information might require investigation.
subfiles.summary: Briggs reports Major Holliman thinks investigation may be needed into why Mate wanted information about the station.

subfiles.title: Referral of the Mate correspondence to the Army
subfiles.from: Francis Colt de Wolf, Department of State
subfiles.to: Lieutenant Colonel C. W. Janes, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Forwards Mate's correspondence to the Army for whatever action it considers appropriate.
subfiles.summary: De Wolf sends Colonel Janes the Kyodo correspondence for the Army to take appropriate action and report.

subfiles.title: Notice to Mate that his inquiry was referred to the Army
subfiles.from: Francis Colt de Wolf, Department of State
subfiles.about: Tells Mate that the Army will answer his questions about Kyodo directly.
subfiles.summary: Department tells Mate his January 15 request was referred to the Army, which administers the occupation, and a direct reply will follow.

subfiles.title: Japanese radio-station publications effective January 1, 1949
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits official lists of Japanese ship, coastal, marine-beacon, fixed, and land radio stations.
subfiles.summary: Acting Political Adviser sends five copies each of two Japanese Ministry of Communications publications listing radio stations authorized by SCAP through January 1, 1949.

subfiles.title: Proposal to resume Japanese international broadcasting
subfiles.from: Huston, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Seeks the Department's views on resuming limited, SCAP-supervised Japanese international broadcasting.
subfiles.summary: Occupation headquarters proposes resuming international broadcasting to advance Japan's international responsibilities, rehabilitate communications, support frequency claims, inform Japanese abroad and spread non-Communist news, initially limited and under supervision.

subfiles.title: Approval of resumed Japanese broadcasting and rejection of VOA use
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Approves renewed Japanese broadcasting but advises against Voice of America use of Japanese shortwave facilities.
subfiles.summary: Department approves resumed Japanese broadcasting with supervision as remote as possible, and finds VOA use of Japanese shortwave facilities inadvisable for now.

subfiles.title: Urgent request for the Department's broadcasting views
subfiles.from: SCAP, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Requests an urgent response because final recommendations on international broadcasting were being prepared.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo refers to its May 5 telegram concerning resumed Japanese international broadcasting. Headquarters was already formulating final recommendations and urgently requested the Department's views.

subfiles.title: Civilian recollection of a Japanese broadcast before Pearl Harbor
subfiles.from: Mr. and Mrs. J. C. Stuart
subfiles.about: Reports hearing a clear Japanese woman's voice on the radio near Los Altos on the night before the attack on Pearl Harbor.
subfiles.summary: The Stuarts recall hearing a Japanese woman speak or chant for a long time the evening before Pearl Harbor and wonder if it held a warning.

subfiles.title: Transmittal cover for Japanese radio-station list
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Serves as the Foreign Service cover and routing sheet for the enclosed July 1949 Japanese radio-station directory.
subfiles.summary: Transmittal cover for a Japanese radio-station list from the Political Adviser's office, dated September 23, 1949.

subfiles.title: List of Japanese Ship and Coastal Radio Stations, 1 July 1949
subfiles.from: Radio Regulatory Agency, Ministry of Telecommunications
subfiles.about: Provides schedules and technical registers for Japanese frequency standards, coastal stations, radiobeacons, and ship radio stations.
subfiles.summary: The directory begins with standard-frequency and time-signal schedules for Tokyo-area and Chōshi transmitters, explanatory charts, and procedures for navigational warnings. It then lists coastal, marine-beacon, and government railroad-ferry beacon stations with coordinates, call signs, frequencies, emissions, power, hours, and operating notes. The ship registry section defines abbreviations and frequency groups before listing vessels by SCAP number, port, tonnage, operational agent, call sign, authorized frequencies, and type; the surviving section covers Niigata and large portions of Ibaraki and Chiba prefectures.
